instrument.name: Federal funds target range
instrument.explainer: The federal funds target range is where the Federal Reserve wants the overnight rate between banks to trade. The Federal Open Market Committee sets it eight times a year in pursuit of maximum employment and 2% inflation. Prime-linked borrowing moves with it almost at once.

eras.note: A single target rate until 15 Dec 2008.
A target range with both bounds since 16 Dec 2008.

transmission.note: Credit cards and home equity lines are priced off the bank prime rate, which has sat 3 points above the target range's upper bound.
A fixed-rate mortgage does not change with the Fed. New mortgage rates follow longer-term bond yields rather than the target directly.
